title: Check
description: One rule the engine applies, kept as a record: Lathe's in its own shipped data, a product's own in the product's data. Its query reads the typed records and reports each problem; the problems of a run are never stored.

title: Product setting
description: A product's settings that its checks read, one record per product: today the most children of one kind a record should hold.

title: Page
description: One place in the app, identified by its address: the products picker (`/`), a record at its bare ID (`/<id>`, a product's and a domain's being their overview), or a group of the graph's tree (a stage or folder, `/<domain-id>/<stage>/<folder>`, or a record's children of one kind, `/<parent-id>/<kind>`); with the tools open over its stage in its query: Checks (`?panel=checks`), Appearance (`?panel=appearance`), the theme editor (`?panel=theme&theme=<id>`), and the reference, a kind's or a check's page in the wiki card (`?page=format`, `?page=format/kinds/<kind>`, `?page=format/checks/<check>`). Every page shows a view of one loaded workspace.
notes:
A product, domain, record or group page shows its one focus on one stage, full window: Graph, ERD (on a domain, aggregate or entity page) or Trace (where an obligation is). The address names it, as in `?stage=erd`; the stage never changes the path. Over the stage float the navigation, the tab panel (the page bar and the header strip) and the wiki card with the focus's wiki page and facts. A format page has no stage: one panel right of the nav, the kind's or check's facts in the page itself.

A record's page reads that data through its aggregate's own queries and changes it only through its aggregate's own commands: its Edit, Add and Remove actions, in the wiki card, send one command each to the server, and the change is reviewed in git like any other.

title: Space
description: One product as a place to work in, kept apart from every other: the pages that belong to it (the Checks panel over them showing its problems alone), its icon, its place among the other spaces, and the last page visited in it. Nothing of another product shows inside a space. The current space is always the product of the page in hand.

title: Nav entry
description: An entry of the nav that folds, a domain, a stage, a kind group or a record with children, and whether the reader has it folded, for the browser session.

title: Tab set
description: The places open at once in one space as tabs side by side with one active, as in a browser: each tab is a place, its focus, stage, camera, depth, kind filters, the wiki card's open and expanded state and scroll, and its own Back and Forward history. Moving never leaves the tab, and a record may be open in several tabs, each its own place. On the web the browser holds the tabs: each browser tab is one place, its focus and stage in the address, its history the browser's, and its view kept for the session (LA-V103-R10).

title: Session settings
description: How the Reader likes to see things, not where they are: the graph's layout (Tree, Nested or Map), whether the minimap shows and the Map draws all its links, and the wiki card's width. One for the reader's browser session, shared by every tab and every place, so moving, opening or switching tabs never changes it. Where the Reader is, depth, kind filters and the wiki card's open state included, is the place's (LA-EXP-A5).

title: View
description: A place in the app where flow steps happen: its requirements with their tests.

title: Endpoint
description: An operation exposed over the network: its requirements with their tests, and its handler.

title: Integration
description: Another system a product exchanges with: its adapter, its tests and the use cases it performs on its own.

title: UI component
description: A piece of the interface that renders views and builds the view requirements its code does.

title: Read model
description: A shape of data a domain reads: its fields, the aggregates it reads, its queries and their handlers, and its projection. Where it is stored is its table's (A18).

title: Storage requirement
description: What the business needs kept of one aggregate or read model, and how well (durability, atomicity, retention and deletion, recovery, capacity), with the storage requirement tests that prove it. It sits under the aggregate or read model it is about, which belongs to another aggregate, so it is an aggregate of its own, as an endpoint is.

title: Domain
description: A business capability of a product: its terms, its capabilities in order, its domain services with what implements and proves them, and its repositories.

title: Specification
description: A rule that decides whether a record satisfies it, with its predicate and its test.

title: Aggregate
description: A consistency boundary of a domain: its entities and their fields and data models, and its invariants with the rules that enforce them and their tests.

title: Domain event
description: Something that happened to an aggregate: its fields and the event type that delivers it.

title: Command
description: An intent to change an aggregate: its handler, the other aggregates it records as changing in its transaction, and the policies it runs, with their handlers and tests.

title: Value object
description: A value with no identity of its own: its fields, its constraints with their tests, and the value type that implements it.

title: Product repo
description: The repo `lathe init` sets up, whose config names its data folder.

title: Shell settings
description: The desktop shell's own settings, kept in a settings file: the editor Open in editor uses, its custom command, and the path to Claude.

title: Key bindings
description: The keys a person gave the app's shortcuts in place of the defaults, which stay in code (the keymap's commands). Only a changed shortcut is kept; one put back to its defaults is dropped again. They change together because no two shortcuts may share a key where both apply: binding one key can take it from another shortcut (a swap).

title: Voice settings
description: How the Owner talks to the desktop chat: voice activation (listen for the wake phrase while the window is in front), Quick mode (send a dictated message by itself once they have finished), the wake phrase, and each voice command's words. They change together because no two phrases may say the same thing; both modes are off until the Owner turns them on.

title: Window chat
description: A product window's chat with Claude Code: the session it runs, its permission mode, model and effort, the messages waiting to go and its listening for the voice, while its window is open; and each folder's last mode, kept for its next chat.

title: Agent sign-in
description: Whether the chat's agent, the Owner's own Claude Code, is being signed in or out from inside the app: the sign-in under way, with the link it gives and whether it asks for a code, or how the last one ended; and whether a sign-out is under way. One for the shell, as the agent keeps one sign-in for every folder. The agent keeps the credentials and says itself whether it is signed in, so Lathe keeps none.

title: Panel
description: A part of the app floating over the stage that a person shows, hides and resizes: the nav and the wiki card. Hiding a panel gives its room to the stage and loses nothing.

title: Appearance
description: The person's themes, the theme chosen, the color mode, and Scroll to zoom: whether scroll zooms the stages' cameras or pans them. How the person likes to see Lathe, the same in every tab and from one launch to the next.

title: Product window
description: A desktop window showing one product folder, with its saved place and the server it loads Lathe from.

title: App server
description: What a window loads Lathe from: `serve()` in the shell's own process, the app's Vite dev server that the shell starts, or the owner's dev server on port 5199, which it only shares. `lathe serve` runs the same `serve()`.

title: Recent folders
description: The folders opened last, latest first, which one list serves every window.

title: Product
description: A product: its roles, its open questions, and the kinds and relations it declares as its own. Its interfaces are aggregates of their own (LA-PRD-A24).

title: Business outcome
description: A measurable change a product exists to bring about, with the tests and records that measure it.

title: Extension record
description: A record of a kind a product declares as its own: its fields, the links it starts and the packages it uses, held to its kind's declaration.

title: Interface
description: A way a product is used, such as an app a person works in, calls other programs make, or a command line: the roles of its product that use it, in order, and the use cases it offers. It changes apart from its product, whose roles it names; the patterns it follows, and the values it gives their settings, are Pattern following's (LA-TRC-A3).

title: Journey
description: An ordered string of use cases and handoffs from a trigger to a result a business outcome measures: its steps on a main path and alternate paths, the use case or policy each carries out, its one journey test, and the outcomes it serves.

title: Table
description: Where an entity's or read model's records, or a domain's own infrastructure such as a link table, are stored: its storage and name, and its keys in order.

title: Entry point
description: A start-up file of a domain, with the packages it uses and the standard rules it meets.

title: Tooling
description: A dev script or config file of a domain, with the packages it uses, the standard rules it meets and the technical records it generates.

title: Data store
description: Where a product's data actually lives (a data server, a bucket, a folder of files, browser storage, memory), under its product or one of its domains. The repositories, readers and tables stored in it name it themselves, and what provides it, when someone else runs it, is its provision (LA-TRC-A5).

title: Standard
description: Rules that hold across the product, each standard a quality (essential) or engineering (accidental), with the rules themselves.

title: Pattern following
description: A domain or use case that follows a pattern, and the value it gives each of the pattern's settings. Which rules each domain owes because of it is worked out (RM04), never stored.

title: Slot filling
description: A technical record, written by hand, that fills a slot of a pattern: a fill, accidental complexity recorded at the slot it is owed to, and debt until the pattern can derive it.

title: Provision
description: What provides a record from outside the product (a dependency, a platform or a generic subdomain), which decides it once for everyone who uses it: a provided record is accounted for, and a provided obligation built and proved, through its provider. One provider per record.

title: Test data set
description: What some tests start from, in one domain: its environment, accounts and records, how to prepare and reset it, and the file that builds it.

title: Use case
description: A goal someone reaches: its actors, its requirements with their tests, and its one flow, the same through every interface that offers it, with its steps and its test.

title: Pattern
description: Behavior several use cases share, written once: its rules, its settings, the value each follower gives a setting, each rule's tests per following domain, and its slots.
